Anglerfish: Keep the true short lure attached continuously to the forehead; all fin bases attached visibly to the body; no loose glow dots or background objects.
Beaked Whale: Show the true narrow beak as a continuous part of the head and two pectoral flippers at separate readable roots; horizontal tail flukes, no extra fins. The male tusk pair must erupt UPWARD from the LOWER jaw; no downward upper-jaw fangs. Keep tooth bases visibly joined to the lower jaw.
Blue Whale: Keep the long body in a calm horizontal swim with both real flippers separated below the front torso and the modest dorsal fin and flukes attached; no detached appendages.
Catfish: Expose both broad pectoral fins at their true roots below the head and keep whisker barbels separate without crossing the fins; show a clearly closed jaw contour.
Dragonfish: Show a readable lower jaw and attached barbel, all fin roots continuous; avoid detached dots or exaggerated threadlike projections.
Eagle Ray: Use a shallow top-side oblique view with the true broad pectoral disc and a long attached thin whip tail. Do not invent a fish caudal fin.
Fangtooth: Closed or only slightly open mouth keeps the tooth-bearing jaw contour clear; retain the characteristic large teeth without external spikes or unconnected paint.
Flying Fish: Keep the two large pectoral flight fins distinct at their true roots with clear fin membranes, a readable tail fork, and no detached rays.
Flying Gurnard: Show a continuous closed jaw and the broad attached winglike pectoral fins with no overlap over the head.
Gray Whale: True rounded head continuous with body; two real flippers with distinct roots; no invented dorsal fin.
Gulper Eel: Preserve the naturally very long tapering body and tail and large hinged mouth. Do not thicken the distal body into an ordinary fish.
Humpback Whale: Two very long pectoral flippers with clearly separated roots, natural tubercles and horizontal flukes; keep every appendage attached.
Lamprey: Keep the naturally finless paired-limb anatomy, long eel body and circular sucker mouth; no invented paired fins or legs. Paint exactly SEVEN individually visible gill pores in one countable row behind the eye; the first painting only showed six.
Lancelet: Preserve true lancelet anatomy: translucent narrow fishlike body with continuous low median fin fold, pointed ends, no invented paired pectoral fins or jaws.
Lionfish: Prior finished film retained key-colour fringe (70 magenta pixels) in the fin/spine structures. Keep natural identifying stripes and translucent fins; paint no magenta tint in animal tissue.
Lungfish: Preserve the real filamentous paired fins and long continuous rear fin; expose the jaw contour without adding a broad ordinary-fish tail.
Manatee: Rounded blunt snout continuous with head; two attached foreflippers and round paddle tail, no dorsal fin.
Manta Ray: Preserve real broad winglike pectoral disc, paired cephalic lobes at the mouth and thin tail. Do not invent a fish caudal fin.
Marlin: Keep the true long bill continuous with a clearly readable head, body and dorsal sail; natural bill length, no detached tip.
Moray Eel: Long slender eel body with continuous dorsal fin, no paired pectoral fins; preserve natural taper and attached jaw.
Narwhal: One long straight tusk attached naturally to the upper jaw, two true pectoral flippers and horizontal flukes; no dorsal fin. Intake refused caudal/body proportion: preserve clearly readable horizontal flukes and their natural tapering peduncle; do not let the tusk be mistaken for a tail. No enlarging or shrinking beyond natural narwhal proportions.
Oarfish: Long narrow ribbon body, continuous red dorsal fin and attached head crest and pelvic rays, all attachments legible without disconnected fragments.
Pilot Whale: Rounded melon smoothly continuous with the head and back, two distinct true flippers, hooked dorsal fin and horizontal flukes.
Pipefish: Prior finished film retained key-colour fringe (10 magenta pixels) on the thin appendages. Keep its true thin shape and attached fins with clean natural-colour edges.
Ray: Shallow top-side oblique view exposes the two sides of the real pectoral disc and the continuous attached tail; no invented ordinary fish fins.
Seahorse: Keep the true upright seahorse posture, tubular snout, continuous plated trunk and curled attached tail, real small fins only.
Stingray: Expose the true broad pectoral disc and continuous thin tail with its natural barb; no invented ordinary fish tail fin.
Tripod Fish: Show the three true long supporting fin rays continuous with their fin bases, as fins rather than jointed legs; preserve the real elongated head and tail. Previous candidate invented three jointed legs with foot-like pads. Paint true slender uninterrupted fin rays: the paired pelvic fin rays and a caudal ray form the tripod. No knees, ankles, toes, foot pads or ground shadows; preserve the canonical fish anatomy. Candidate two still put the rear support ray on the belly: the single rear support MUST extend from the CAUDAL TAIL FIN at the far left, not the belly. Only the paired pelvic rays arise below the body.
Whale: Whole horizontal whale with true rounded head continuous into torso, two readable flipper roots, dorsal fin if canonical species facts require it and attached flukes.
Ant: Right-facing ant, head and jaws at right and abdomen left, six real legs with separate readable roots and feet, two elbowed antennae; no far legs merged into the abdomen.
Black Fly: Right-facing black fly with six small legs, true short antennae and natural mouthparts. Do not invent large beetle mandibles for a small biting fly.
River Dolphin: Prior finished film retained key-colour fringe (14 magenta pixels) around head/body. Paint a continuous rounded melon and throat with clean attached contours, no pink key residue or detached skin slivers.
